questions.question: Identify any two barriers to good communication.
questions.solution_html:
• Two common barriers to effective communication are
  • a) Physical Barriers : These are obstacles in the environment that interfere with the transmission
  • of a message. Examples: Noise, distance, poor lighting, or any environmental condition that
  • disrupts communication.
  • b) Psychological Barriers: These relate to the emotional or mental state of the communicator
  • which affects how messages are sent or received.
  • Examples: Stress, fear, anxiety,preconceived notions, or emotional bias.
  • Read (Manuscript Mode): The speaker reads the entire speech word-for-word from a prepared text.
  • It is used when absolute accuracy of language and data is required. Example: A newsreader reads
  • the news script.
  • Visual aids should be used as tools to help the audience understand the information better and
  • faster. They must make your speech clear, interesting, and memorable.
  • Overcrowding: Do not use charts or slides with too many lines or small text, as they become difficult
  • to read quickly.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: to read quickly.

questions.question: Define the main goals of public speaking and list its four primary purposes.
questions.solution_html:
• The main goal of public speaking is to communicate messages clearly to a group. The four primary

  • Example: Delivering a class presentation or a business meeting speech.

questions.question: Describe how public speaking is different from casual conversation.
questions.solution_html:
• Public speaking (speaking to a group) differs from casual conversation (talking to one person) in these
  • key ways
  • • Interaction: Public speaking involves limited interaction and is mostly one-way, while conversation
  • is direct and personal, a two-way exchange.
  • • Preparation: Public speaking requires planning, organization, and practice, while conversation is
  • usually spontaneous.
  • • Tone and Language: Public speaking is typically formal or semi -formal and structured, while
  • conversation is informal and conversational.
  • • Feedback: Feedback in public speaking is often delayed or generalized (from audience reactions)
  • while in conversation, it is immediate.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: while in conversation, it is immediate.

questions.question: Describe how to choose a simple and interesting topic for a speech.
questions.solution_html:
• Selecting a Speech Topic
  • Choosing a speech topic is the first and most important step in preparing a good speech. A good topic should
  • be interesting to you and relevant to the audience. Pick something you know about or are willing to learn more
  • about. The topic should also match the purpose of your speech—whether it is to inform, persuade, or entertain.
  • • Personal interest – Choose something you enjoy, like music or travel. Example: If you like cooking, you
  • can speak about “Healthy Snacks for Students.”
  • • Audience interest – Pick a topic suitable for the listeners. Example: For classmates, “Time Management
  • for Students” works well.
  • • Knowledge level – Select a topic you understand. If you know about sports, choose “Benefits of Playing
  • Football.”
  • Research also helps you choose a good speech topic because it shows whether there is enough correct
  • information available. By checking books, websites, and talking to people, you can find out which topics
  • you can explain easily. It also helps you pick a topic that is interesting and true, so your speech becomes
  • clear and trustworthy.
  • A clear topic makes the speech easier to prepare and deliver.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: A clear topic makes the speech easier to prepare and deliver.
